title: Public BTC futures: open-interest crash, rebound and weak taker-flow event test
question: Does an independently specified short filter following a past OI decline, negative prior return and unconfirmed positive rebound show positive test PNL or incremental PNL over a validation-chosen baseline? Training July-August 2024, selection September, final test October-December, all fixed before performance inspection. One unit initial notional per separate 30-minute short; arithmetic, not compounded, PNL. The independent check shares input samples and selected thresholds but separately reconstructs masks and fee-adjusted PNL. The checksum source concerns archive bytes only.

hypotheses.statement: The validation-selected full OI/rebound/flow filter has positive mean daily arithmetic test PNL after one-basis-point cost per leg and realized fixed-notional funding accrual.
hypotheses.falsifier: The circular seven-day-block bootstrap 95% interval for mean test daily PNL lies wholly below zero. An interval including zero, fewer than twenty test trades, or no eligible validation candidate is inconclusive.

hypotheses.statement: The full filter has positive incremental mean daily test PNL over the reference chosen solely on validation among cash, price-only, OI-only and flow-only baselines at the same per-trade notional; exposure need not be equal.
hypotheses.falsifier: The paired seven-day-block bootstrap 95% interval for incremental daily PNL lies wholly below zero. Zero-containing intervals or the H1 sample-size gates are inconclusive.

hypotheses.statement: Negative economic control: increasing the per-leg trading fee from one to five basis points, with exactly the same trade decisions, increases total arithmetic test PNL.
hypotheses.falsifier: At least one trade is present and the higher fee lowers total PNL by its exact fee difference; no trades means inconclusive.
